events.title: Grand Vision
events.summary: Visiting artist Olayami Dabls is a storyteller, curator, educator, and mentor. He is the founder of the MBAD African Bead Museum in Detroit. Through material culture, Dabls presents commentary on the past, present, and future from African and African-American perspectives, with the understanding that generations of African ancestors used visual materials to convey information about their identity as well as send messages for healing and protection. Dabls is a luminary; for decades he has re-imagined what a museum space can be, accessible to everyone, free from the underpinnings of colonialism and the Western, often white, frame. *Grand Vision* includes a conceptual installation in the Gallery, presenting Dabls’s own work in visual conversation with African beads and artifacts from Dabls’s Bead Museum collections. Additionally, Dabls’s iconic outdoor sculpture *Iron Teaching Rocks Table Manners* will be installed on the U-M campus grounds near UMMA, at the intersection of State Street and South University from September 17- October 11, 2026. The project’s range intends to more fully articulate the many facets of Dabls’ creative practice, and the overlay of art, history, identity, community, and healing.

events.title: Best of FAMU
events.summary: The program of short films offers a representative cross-section of works created at Prague’s film school throughout its eighty-year history. The eight selected films vividly illustrate the diversity of student filmmaking, encompassing fiction, documentary, and animation, as well as both lesser-known works and internationally acclaimed titles (including a Student Academy Award winner). Together, they span a wide range of styles and genres, from pantomime slapstick and historical drama to mockumentary and animated fantasy. The selection includes early works by filmmakers such as Jan Němec and Jan Svěrák, who went on to become major figures in Czech cinema, alongside outstanding talents from younger generations, including Daria Kashcheeva, Bára Anna Stejskalová, and Marie-Magdalena Kochová. List of films: • Encounter • The Loaf of Bread • Oil Gobblers • Closed Due to the Family Mourning • Pripyat Piano • Daughter • Love Is Just a Death Away • 3 MWh Film Synopsis: • Encounter (Vladimír Svitáček, 1953, 5 min.) Vladimír Svitáček, later renowned as a co-creator of the multimedia theatre Laterna Magika and the world’s first interactive movie Kinoautomat, depicts a crowded Prague tram in this pantomime-inspired comic sketch, featuring outstanding performances by the young Miloš Kopecký and Jiří Sovák. The film also includes rare archival footage of the area surrounding Prague’s Main Railway Station. Director: Vladimír Svitáček Screenwriter: Vladimír Svitáček Director of Photography: Jerzy Kotowski Original Score: Jaroslav Ježek Cast: Miloš Kopecký, Jiří Sovák, Jana Werichová-Kvapilová, Káťa Kopecká etc. • The Loaf of Bread (Jan Němec, 1960, 11 min.) This early student film by Jan Němec, one of the leading figures of the Czech New Wave, can be regarded as a thematic precursor to his masterpiece Diamonds of the Night. In the final days of the Second World War, a train carrying concentration camp prisoners stands at a railway station. Three exhausted inmates contemplate how to reach a nearby freight car loaded with bread, hoping to regain enough strength before attempting their escape. Director: Jan Němec Screenwriter: Jan Němec, Eva Límanová Director of Photography: Jiří Šámal Cast: Ivan Renč, Jan Bartůšek, Oldřich Bláha • Oil Gobblers (Jan Svěrák, 1988, 20 min.) Jan Svěrák’s Oil Gobblers was made in 1988 as his graduation film at the Department of Documentary Film. This mockumentary follows a fictional scientific expedition in search of an unknown creature known as the “oil gobbler,” whose very existence defies all the principles of life in a healthy natural environment. The film turns a serious ecological issue completely on its head, presenting its story with such convincing realism that the hoax is almost flawless. In June 1989, the film received the Student Academy Award presented by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences. Director, Screenwriter: Jan Svěrák Director of Photography: Ladislav Štěpán Original Score: Vendula Kašpárková Cast: Lubomír Beneš, Jiří Němec, Ivo Kašpar, Jan Rokyta, Emil Nedbal etc. • Closed Due to the Family Mourning (Saša Gedeon, 1991, 9 min.) This short film by screenwriter and director Saša Gedeon is based on Alberto Moravia’s short story Fire. A bittersweet vignette, it portrays a single day in a small Italian barbershop on the eve of the Second World War. Rather than relying on an intricate plot, the film derives its power from its understated emotional tension and evocative atmosphere. Made during Gedeon’s second year at FAMU, the film received an award at the FFICS – International Festival of Film School Students in Tokyo in 1992. The prize money enabled the director to make his feature-film debut Indian Summer. Director, Screenwriter: Saša Gedeon Director of Photography: Miloš Kabyl Cast: Barbora Hrzánová, David Vávra, Jakub Špalek, Renata Beccerová • Pripyat Piano (Eliška Cílková, 2019, 18 min.) Many of the original inhabitants of Pripyat have never come to terms with the Chernobyl disaster. Some of them began composing their own songs and poems and returning to their apartments within the forbidden radioactive zone. This documentary concert, reflecting on the presence of a unique space, calls for the return of humankind as both creator and performer. In the poems and songs recited by the former residents of Pripyat themselves, a powerful connection between people and home can still be heard to endure. The film has been screened at major documentary film festivals and has received numerous awards. Director, Editor, Original Score, Sound Design: Eliška Cílková Director of Photography: Tomáš Frkal • Daughter (Daria Kashcheeva, 2019, 14 min.) This puppet animation by Daria Kashcheeva tells the story of a father and daughter who, despite mutual misunderstanding, eventually find their way back to each other. The film’s emotional intensity and unsettling atmosphere are enhanced by an unusually dynamic camera – rare in animation – and by close-up shots of the puppets’ faces, whose expressions feel remarkably lifelike. The film won the prestigious Student Academy Award (in the category of international animation) and was nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Short Film. Director, Screenwriter, Director of Photography: Daria Kashcheeva Original Score: Petr Vrba Editor: Alexander Kashcheev • Love Is Just a Death Away (Bára Anna Stejskalová, 2020, 10 min.) A dead dog, a landfill, and beautiful moths high in the sky – this is the world of Steve, a parasite desperately searching for a kindred soul. Yet every attempt at connection ends in disappointment. A small bird he saves from another dog dies. A rat that touches him dies. Cockroaches, under the guise of friendship, strip him down to the bone. Completely defenseless inside the skeleton of his former host, he nearly loses his life under the wheels of a machine that crushes waste. The film has screened at numerous festivals and received the award for Best Student Animated Short Film as well as the Audience Award for Best Animated Short Film at the Palm Springs International Film Festival. Director, Editor, Original Score, Sound Design: Bára Anna Stejskalová Director of Photography: Tomáš Frkal • 3 MWh (Marie-Magdalena Kochová, 2024, 13 min.) An employee at a nuclear power plant, obsessed with counting, sets himself a limit on how much electricity he wants to consume for the rest of his life. In this dark yet masterful cinematic poem shot on 35mm film, Marie-Magdalena Kochová presents the story of a man whose life is moving toward transformation. It is a tender acceptance of the idea that we are not only our bodies, but also energy. The film has been screened at numerous international festivals and Czech Film Critics Award. Director: Marie-Magdalena Kochová Screenwriter: Josef Kokta Director of Photography: Kristina Kůlová Original Score: Haštal Hapka Cast: Jaroslav Pížl

events.title: Shortbus 20th Anniversary Live Commentary Screening w/ John Cameron Mitchell
events.summary: Join John Cameron Mitchell in celebrating the 20th anniversary of his groundbreaking film “SHORTBUS” with a live in-person commentary screening featuring behind the scenes stories of the making of the film! The evening will end with a Q&A and music! Produced by ThisMyShow Presents (A Night In Mission Hill, Sandwiches of History Live!) "SHORTBUS" A group of New Yorkers caught up in their romantic-sexual milieu converge at an underground salon infamous for its blend of art, music, politics, and carnality. John wrote, directed, and starred in the rock musical and film Hedwig and the Angry Inch for which he won the Tony Award for Best Revival of a Musical, a special Tony for his performance, an Obie Award, the Best Director award at the Sundance Festival and a Golden Globe nomination for Best Actor, along with 25 other awards. He wrote and directed the improv-based film Shortbus; directed the film adaptation of Pulitzer Prize-winning play Rabbit Hole, which garnered a Best Actress Oscar nom for Nicole Kidman; and co-wrote and directed the YA punk romance How to Talk to Girls at Parties, starring Kidman and Elle Fanning. He executive-produced (with Gus Van Sant) Jonathan Caouette’s Tarnation, which was the most decorated documentary of 2004. John was in the original casts of Tony-winning Big River, The Secret Garden, and Six Degrees of Separation; as well as Hello Again (Drama Desk nom.) and Larry Kramer’s The Destiny of Me (Obie Award). TV roles include: "Girls," "Shrill," "The Good Fight," "Mozart in the Jungle," "Yellowjackets," "The Sandman," "City on Fire," and Joe Exotic in "Joe vs Carole." He wrote and directed two scripted podcast series: the musical Anthem: Homunculus starring Glenn Close, Cynthia Erivo, Patti Lupone, and Laurie Anderson; and the satirical sitcom Cancellation Island starring Holly Hunter. $35 - General Admission $50 - Priority GA - Seating after VIP and before regular GA $100 - VIP W/ Meet & Greet - First admission and postshow meet and greet with John (photo on personal device, one item to be signed) Show at 7pm VIP seating starts at 6:15 Priority GA seating at 6:30 General Admission seating at 6:45

events.title: Faster and More Fun: American Home Cooking in the 1920s
events.summary: Visit the Hatcher Gallery Exhibit Room to see historical materials that illustrate women’s changing relationship with food, cooking, and technology during the heady decade of the 1920s, sandwiched between WWI and the Great Depression. This exhibit features materials from the Janice Bluestein Longone Culinary Archive, as well as select items from the Art, Architecture, and Engineering Special Collections and the Transportation History Collection. As America rang in a new decade in the 1920s, cookbook authors and appliance manufacturers stood ready to offer the newly emancipated and forward-thinking American woman a vision for her future, a vision that would be scientifically grounded, speedy enough to make time for leisure as well as housework, and guaranteed to bring fun to that most humdrum of chores: planning and preparing meals for a family three times a day, 365 days a year.

Viewer discretion is advised. Two lovebirds, Ania and Charles, meet for their first-and-three-quarters date: a home cooked meal. But there is a secret at the table: one of them eats people. The other, of course, is fully aware, because the one who eats people – Ania – is an ancient vampire, while the other – Charles – hunts and eats vampires alive. When these forces – life, and unlife – go for each other’s throats, who will go home with a full stomach? This two act, four-course horror/thriller highlights legacy, cannibalism, the inevitability of personal failure, and the complex moral nature of predation in all its incarnations. events.title: Visualizing Care: Storytelling as Data Visualization at MohenjoDaro
events.summary: Set in the World Heritage Site of MohenjoDaro (Sindh, Pakistan), Visualizing Care approaches archaeological data visualization through deep mapping. Experimenting with multimodal and accessible forms of archaeological data presentation, this study explores how care through time can be documented. Within an archaeological context, the materiality of care can be seen through the intentional making/unmaking of urban design, architectural features, and infrastructure. Within a historical and contemporary framework, care can be visualized through conservation and the relationships between caretakers and the site itself, drawing attention to the affective aspects of archaeological research. This transdisciplinary project utilizes archival material, LiDAR and 3-dimensional artifact captures, ethnographic conversations, GIS mapping, sound, and experiments with mudbrick, to explore the many different ways of knowing the ancient city of MohenjoDaro. Uzma Z. Rizvi is Professor of Anthropology and Urban Studies, in the Department of Social Science and Cultural Studies, Pratt Institute, Brooklyn, NY. She is also a visiting faculty at Shah Abdul Latif University in Khairpur, Pakistan. Dr. Rizvi’s work intentionally interweaves archaeology with cultural criticism, philosophy, critical theory, art, and design. With over two decades of work on decolonizing methodologies, intersectional and feminist strategies, and transdisciplinary approaches, her work has intentionally pushed disciplinary limits, and demanded ethical decolonial praxis at all levels of engagement, from teaching to research. She is the PI of the Laboratory for Integrated Archaeological Visualization and Heritage (liavh.org), currently working at the 3rd millennium BCE world heritage site of MohenjoDaro, Pakistan. The lecture begins at 4PM EST, in person at the Kelsey Museum (Room 125). Reception to follow at 5:30PM. If you are unable to attend in person, you may view the lecture via zoom by registering here: https://umich.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_Kai9ybzNSoGPYxwjs6lAyQ#/registration

events.title: Baird Carillon Rededication Recital
events.summary: Experience the return of the landmark 53-bell Charles Baird Carillon, which went silent this summer for replacement of the 30 largest clappers as well as a restoration of the great steel frame from which the 43 tons of bells are suspended. Guest artist Jonathan Lehrer, University Carillonist of Grand Valley State University and Michigan State University, will perform the rededication recital, beginning with the first full performance of "The Victors" on the Baird Carillon since the 2017 U-M Bicentennial as a duet with U-M University Carillonist Tiffany Ng. "The Victors" will also be livestreamed to SMTD's YouTube channel. Lehrer's program includes "To The Sun," an interactive 10-minute performance for carillon and audience cell phones celebrating data from NASA's Parker Solar Probe. The U-M Frankel Detroit Observatory will coordinate a solar observation station at the base of the carillon throughout the recital, weather permitting. Their solar telescope provides magnificent views of sunspots, prominences, and more. The outdoor audience listening space is Ingalls Mall, and listeners are advised to dress for the weather. Tours of the bell chamber will begin after the conclusion of the recital around 4:00 pm. The bell chamber may be accessed via a combination of elevator and stairs, and is not ADA accessible. *This event is supported by an Arts Initiative Project Support (AIPS) grant.* GUEST ARTIST BIO JON LEHRER is the sixth University Carillonist of Michigan State University and the second University Carillonist of Grand Valley State University. A laureate of five international competitions for carillon (including the Queen Fabiola, the Nederlandse Klokkenspel Vereniging, and the Alexius Julien Baroque competitions), he is now a prolific soloist on the global stage, with a CV that includes touring overseas on behalf of the Canada Council for the Arts, teaching masterclasses at Universities across the nation, and performing hundreds of shows on the North American renaissance festival circuit. Jon studied carillon with Geert D’Hollander, Eddy Marien, Koen Cosaert, and Ellen Dickenson and holds degrees from Yale University and the Royal Carillon School of Belgium. Having recently retired from data science and cancer research, he is focused on creating moments of beauty for busy university communities, growing the carillon art, and helping to train the next generation of expressive carillon virtuosi. Jon lives in Michigan with his partner Christy and their two cat-café adoptees, Henry and Juliet.

events.title: Grand Vision
events.summary: Visiting artist Olayami Dabls is a storyteller, curator, educator, and mentor. He is the founder of the MBAD African Bead Museum in Detroit. Through material culture, Dabls presents commentary on the past, present, and future from African and African-American perspectives, with the understanding that generations of African ancestors used visual materials to convey information about their identity as well as send messages for healing and protection. Dabls is a luminary; for decades he has re-imagined what a museum space can be, accessible to everyone, free from the underpinnings of colonialism and the Western, often white, frame. *Grand Vision* includes a conceptual installation in the Gallery, presenting Dabls’s own work in visual conversation with African beads and artifacts from Dabls’s Bead Museum collections. Additionally, Dabls’s iconic outdoor sculpture *Iron Teaching Rocks Table Manners* will be installed on the U-M campus grounds near UMMA, at the intersection of State Street and South University from September 17- October 11, 2026. The project’s range intends to more fully articulate the many facets of Dabls’ creative practice, and the overlay of art, history, identity, community, and healing.

events.title: Everything I Want to Do In a Show | A One Woman Show
events.summary: Hi, I'm Heather Sejnow. You may remember me from such things as that Christmas Commercial for a toy store that gets played every year near St. Claire Shores; hosting shows at the Senate or Redford Theatre as dead celebrities or film characters; or living in Chicago for a short while to do Second City, iO, and then hop back to Detroit to perform at Go Comedy and Planet Ant. I've even nabbed the title of the only female stand up impressionist in the state of Michigan ( that I know of) . I haven't been on a real theatrical performance stage in a while and I'm about to turn 40. So for my mid-life crisis I'm putting on a show of "Everything I Want to Do in a Show". It's campy, crazy, and heartfelt. Most importantly, it's a love letter to everyone I've met and all the vessels of creativity I've learned along the way. Oh! And it's interactive, NSFW, and there will be some prizes for attendees. So come join me on a wild ride filled with puppets, impressions, burlesque, song, dance, and even Shakespeare. It's definitely... "Everything".

events.title: Murray Hill – Showbiz! The Tour
events.summary: Celebrating the release of his debut memoir Showbiz! My Life as a Middle-Aged Man, comedian Murray Hill hits the road with a one-of-a-kind show that is part cabaret, part stand-up, and part behind-the-curtain tell-all. The self-proclaimed “hardest working middle-aged man in show business” brings his signature mix of razor-sharp wit, rampant ad-libbing, and heartfelt storytelling to the stage for a night of big laughs and hard-won wisdom from an outsider who made it his way. \n
